Over the years as she got so grotesquely huge, it became really difficult to be around her. I mean, just the initial sight of her after being away from her for months or years, and I would always be appalled, shocked, and aghast at how much larger she had gotten. I cringed imagining the severe damage that was going on internally, and frankly I figured she would die young, but I thought it would be after a lot of hospitalizations and whatnot.

No, instead she died in her sleep one night completely out of the blue, no one expecting it. It was horrible. Now I struggle with the ambivalence of feeling furious that she was so cavalier about her weight when everyone else around her was anything but... but also feeling intense sadness and grief, and missing her every moment.

I'm not sure I have anything helpful to say about how I dealt with (still dealing with) her death because when she died, it set into motion a cascade of events that resulted in my elderly parents relocating across the country to be near me (they had lived near my late sister), so I am still pretty distracted by all the shit I've had to do to help make that happen.

Anyway, I know what a lot of people told me, which was just to be patient with the process, don't have any preconceived expectations of how "long" it should take you to "get over it", and seek therapy or a group support option if you feel it may be beneficial. Hope you're doing OK today.
